title: Roasted Chicken Jus with Shallot, Thyme & Dijon
description: Roasted chicken jus brightened with white wine, sweet shallot, thyme, and a restrained touch of Dijon. Made for pork tenderloin or chicken.
ingredients: 350 mL unsalted roasted chicken jus, without finishing butter (see Roasted Chicken Jus)
10 g Dijon mustard (about 2 teaspoons), plus up to 5 g more to taste
20 g cold unsalted butter, cubed, for finishing
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
A few drops of lemon juice or white wine vinegar, only if needed
steps: Melt 10 g butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the shallot and soften for 3–4 minutes without browning.
Add the wine and thyme. Simmer until the wine is reduced to about 2 tablespoons and its harsh alcoholic aroma has mellowed.

Add the prepared jus and simmer gently for 5–10 minutes, until concentrated and lightly coating a spoon. If the jus was already very concentrated, warm it without much further reduction and add a little water as needed.
Remove the thyme. For a smooth sauce, strain out the shallot; otherwise leave it in.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in 10 g Dijon, then the cold butter a few cubes at a time. Taste before adding any remaining mustard.
Season with salt and pepper. Add a few drops of lemon juice or vinegar only if needed. Serve warm over chicken or pork.
notes: This is a house variation, not a separate classical mother sauce. Keep the mustard in the background so the roasted chicken remains the main flavor. Timing assumes prepared jus; making the jus from scratch adds about 4½–5½ hours. For a pan sauce, soften the shallot in the pan used to cook the meat after pouring off excess fat, then deglaze with wine and follow the remaining steps. Avoid a hard boil after adding the finishing butter.
